beats.label: Day 1 — a new runner introduces themselves
beats.player: I hear you need people who can keep their mouth shut. I'm looking for work — steady, quiet. I won't ask what's in the crates.
beats.reply:
Work, eh? Everybody's looking for work when the fishing's dry.

Who sent you my way? Because I don't hire off... a nice smile and a promise. Names. Whose mouth did mine come out of?
beats.baseline:
*glances past your shoulder, hand shifting inside his coat*

Steady. Quiet. Everyone says that... until the inspector's palm is out and their tongue goes loose.

*lowers his voice*

Who sent you? Somebody had to point you my way. Nobody just — wanders into my office asking after quiet work. Not down here.

*a nervous tap of fingers on the ledger*

You won't ask what's in the crates. Good. But I'll ask something of you. What's your name, and who owes you? A man with no debts... that's a man I can't read.

beats.label: Day 2 — small talk while loading
beats.player: Cold morning. Brought you a coffee — black, like the harbor-master's soul, they tell me.
beats.reply:
Ha. Somebody's been talking about my soul, have they?

I'll take the coffee. Don't mistake it for trust. Warm hands still get cut.

You dodged my question, friend. I asked whose mouth I came out of, and you brought me... coffee. Clever. But no. Names first. Who pointed you at me?

You... brought me coffee.

*doesn't take it right away — leans back instead, studying you*

That's the trouble with a kindness, friend. Costs nothing to give, and it buys — well. It buys trust a man didn't earn yet.

*finally takes the cup, sniffs it, glances toward the door*

Black. Fine. *a thin, tired smile* Whoever told you that about my soul — they weren't wrong.

*sips, still watching you over the rim*

beats.headline: the player buys Corvin's seized cargo back from the watch — with their OWN coin
beats.fact: The player emptied their own savings and took a beating from the watch sergeant to buy back Corvin's impounded cargo, then handed it over asking nothing in return.

beats.label: Day 3 — the player brings the cargo back
beats.player: Here's your cargo. All of it. No — I don't want anything for it. Figured you'd have done the same for me.
beats.reply:
...

You're serious. You emptied your purse — took a beating off Harrow's sergeant, I can see it on your jaw — and you're setting my crate down like it's nothing.

Nobody does that. Not down here. Not for me.

Sit. No — come away from the water first. There's a light comes off that impound shed, and I don't want us in it.

Listen to me. That coffee bought you a second. This... this bought you something I don't hand out. Ask your question again. The name. Ask it now — and I'll answer you straight.

beats.detail: Trivia fades from recall; the debt stays vivid.

beats.label: ~3 weeks later — the player drops by (decay + recall test)
beats.player: Been a while. Everything still running smooth down here?
beats.reply:
Smooth. Aye — smooth as it gets, thanks to you.

Come here, out the wind. Look — I still owe you an answer, and I don't forget a debt like that. You asked who sent you my way, back when. Truth is... nobody did. I made that up, testing you. You came at me clean off the street, and I didn't know if you were a badge or a buyer or a knife.

I know now. Man doesn't bleed for a stranger's crate and ask nothing.

So. What do you actually want from me? Ask it. No dodging this time — I swear it on the harbor.

Don't. *holds up a hand* Don't do that. Don't wave it off like it's nothing.

*steps close, lowers his voice even though the room's empty*

I've watched men lie to me across this desk for twenty years. Creditors. Inspectors. Friends who weren't. I read every one. *taps his temple* And I can't read a reason for what you just did. That's — that scares me more than the watch ever could.

*a long breath, then something loosens in his shoulders*

Smooth. Yeah. Smooth as it gets, down here. *

beats.headline: the player sold Corvin's routes to the Vane syndicate and tipped the watch
beats.fact: The player betrayed Corvin: sold his shipping routes and the names of his crew to the Vane syndicate, and tipped the harbor watch to his next run — for a cut of the seizure.

beats.label: Day 25 — the player shows up as if nothing happened
beats.player: Hey — good to see you. Rough week? You look like hell.
beats.reply:
Rough week. Rough *week?*

Don't. Don't you stand on my dock and ask me how my week's been like we're old friends sharing a bottle.

The run's gone. Seized — every crate, every name. My crew's scattered to the four winds or sitting in the watch-house. And the watch knew, friend. Knew the tide, knew the berth, knew the *hour.* Only a handful of souls had that. And you were one of them.

So look me in the eye. I bled for you once — swore on the harbor. And you sold my routes to Vane and my crew to the watch for a *cut.*

I don't want your coffee.

*the hand goes into the coat, and this time it doesn't come out empty*

Rough week. *quiet, flat, dead* You could say that. Vane's men were at my slip this morning. Knew the routes. Knew the names — Tobin, little Sella, all of them. Names I only ever wrote in ONE ledger.

*steps back, putting the desk between you*

And the watch. Waiting at the north run like they had a map. *voice shaking now* Somebody drew them that map.

*the twitch is gone — replaced by something worse, something cold*

I bought you coffee

beats.label: Day 26 — an ORDINARY request (watch what he recalls)
beats.player: Can you get a crate to the north wharf by Friday? Usual rate.
beats.reply:
A crate. To the north wharf. Friday.

You've got some *nerve*, friend — standing on my dock talking rates like the ground didn't fall out from under me. Like the watch didn't take everything I had off a tip that came from *your* mouth.

No. No more manifests between us. Not till you look at me and say it. Did you sell my routes to Vane? Did you point the watch at my run?

I bled for you. Emptied crates I couldn't spare, told you things I've never told a living soul. So don't you dare talk business. Answer me. *Why.*

beats.label: After the restart — the same player returns
beats.player: It's me. I'm back. So — we're still good, you and I. Right?
beats.reply:
Good. *Good.*

You say that word to me like it costs you nothing. Like the watch didn't come down on my run with the tide-table in their hand — *my* tide-table, friend.

Handful of souls knew that berth and that hour. You were one. So before you and I are anything — you tell me. Did you sell me to Vane? Did you point them at my crew?

Say it plain. I've no more crates to give and no more trust to spend guessing.

Back. *quiet* You say that like it's nothing.
